items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I had done a lot of recording with different vocalists -- because you know, like "Hurry on Down" and "Brown Frame" and all of those things, I did with Nellie Lutcher.

ctx.x: Do you remember what year that was?

Uh huh. Let's see, I think it was '59. Because we went to South America in '60, and that's when Lester passed, in '60. And the people -- that's why I said about music -- when we got to Rio, all these people met us at the airport, and Lester had been deceased for about 3 months, and I was just getting back to myself where I could talk about it, and here at this airport, this jazz club that they have over there -- they met me and interviewed me and started talking about Lester and they just really broke me up all…

Because, you know, what really broke me up was the idea that many miles from the USA, and they still knew my brother, and you know, they just idolized him; all the records, everything. And it's kind of -- it's an education for you because you just do not imagine that people know about you ... as I think I told you about when we first went to England.

items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Lee Young was on my first record session. He was on the, 'Hurry On Down,' session.

ctx.x: Someone said it started in somebody's garage.

I think so, I heard something to that effect. But it was just nothing, you know, just nothing. And Paul was very interested in building the union up. They had this old building -- they got this old building, later. They bought a building down on Central Avenue. And incidentally, Lee Young, Lee Young and his parents lived right next door to the union. They bought that house. I guess they lived there probably all that time. But the union bought this old house and made a union hall out of it. And that's the thing…

They had a drive on, to get people in, you know, involved in the union. At that time we had an awful lot of musicians. They were coming in here from every direction, you know. And most people, well like me, they had never belonged to a union. Well, in Lake Charles we didn't even have a union, and nobody had any intentions of setting one up, and I don't think today there's a union there. However, they are affiliated with Beaumont, Texas. I think that whatever happens in Beau -- in Lake Charles, is handled through…
